[earlier · archive] Ernesto Quintero was one of the only players still working. No coaches. No teammates. Just him, a bucket of baseballs, and a swing that looked like it was arguing with itself. Most of the swings were workmanlike. Hard, yes — everything he hits is hard — but routine. Line drives that stayed flat. Ground balls that hopped like they had weight. Nothing uncommon. Then he took one swing that didn’t match the rest. I didn’t see the ball’s path. I heard it. The contact didn’t echo the way it usually does in an empty park.
